request.user:
Change c0116. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. VI.

Context before (unchanged): Justine, thus received in our family, learned the duties of a servant; a condition which, in our fortunate country, does not include the idea of ignorance, and a sacrifice of the dignity of a human being.

1818 text: "After what I have said, I dare say you well remember the heroine of my little tale: for Justine was a great favourite of your's; and I recollect you once remarked, that if you were in an ill-humour, one glance from Justine could dissipate it, for the same reason that Ariosto gives concerning the beauty of Angelica—she looked so frank-hearted and happy.

1831 text: "Justine, you may remember, was a great favourite of yours; and I recollect you once remarked, that if you were in an ill-humour, one glance from Justine could dissipate it, for the same reason that Ariosto gives concerning the beauty of Angelica—she looked so frank-hearted and happy.

Diff: " [-After what I have said-] {+Justine+} , [-I dare say-] you [-well-] {+may+} remember [-the heroine of my little tale: for Justine-] {+,+} was a great favourite of [-your's-] {+yours+} ; and I recollect you once remarked, that if you were in an ill-humour, one glance from Justine could dissipate it, for the same reason that Ariosto gives concerning the beauty of Angelica—she looked so frank-hearted and happy.

Context after (unchanged): My aunt conceived a great attachment for her, by which she was induced to give her an education superior to that which she had at first intended.

result.rationale: The 1831 text drops "After what I have said, I dare say… the heroine of my little tale: for", removing the narrator's self-conscious reference to the story as a "little tale" and its heroine, and simply opens with "Justine, you may remember". Mostly deletion, with some rewording.
